newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal Treasury bonds seen at record low rate.
newsitem.headline: Portugal Treasury bonds seen at record low rate.

text.p: The Treasury was expected to place 10-year Portuguese bonds at a record low interest rate, in line with the secondary market, at today's auction. But dealers were unsure whether the rate would be above or below 6.85 percent.
Results of the auction will be known around 1100 GMT.
"The 10 billion escudos ought to be fully placed and bids will be around 6.85 percent," said a fixed rate director.
An analyst said "There could be bids below 6.85 percent, and the only doubt is whether the bonds will be placed above or below that level."

At the last auction on November 5, the Treasury placed 10 billion escudos of 10-year bonds at a weighted average interest rate of 7.56925 percent. The maximum offered rate was 7.57 percent and the minimum was 7.56 percent.
February 2006 bonds closed on Tuesday on the Continuous Market at 11,758 escudos to yield 6.85 percent with a spread of one basis point below February 2006 Bonos.
